name: Aboriginal Dreamings Gallery
reason: Retail art gallery and shop; the run rules reject a retail gallery even when Wikivoyage and VisitCanberra list it (rule 2: shop).
objection: Three counted sources name it and it exhibits Indigenous art, so a visitor could browse for half an hour; but it is a commercial seller, weekday visits by appointment only.

name: Air CBR helicopter tour
reason: An operator and a flight, not a place (COVERAGE: a spot is a place).
objection: None worth keeping; the places it flies over are separate candidates.

name: Australian Institute of Sport
reason: Wikivoyage (Belconnen, read) names the precinct and visitor centre: free precinct entry, Sportex exhibit and daily 90-minute guided tours; national institution visitors go in (rule 2).
objection: A working training campus; the visit is mostly a paid tour and could be seen as an operator product.

name: Australian National Botanic Gardens
reason: VisitCanberra and Wikivoyage (read) name the gardens as the easiest place to experience the bush, with rainforest to desert plantings and a trail to Black Mountain; national institution, free entry (rules 1-3).
objection: None of substance; its themed gardens are parts of it, not separate spots.

name: Blundells Cottage
reason: Wikivoyage North Canberra (read) lists it: 1860s cottage open Sat-Sun 10-2, with VisitCanberra museums page; a heritage house the public can enter (rule 2).
objection: Small, a 30-minute visit with weekend-only hours.

name: Boer War Memorial
reason: Part of Anzac Parade and a minor memorial (rule 3); no source singles it out as a visit.
objection: It is a named stop for some Anzac Parade walkers, but the avenue is the draw.

name: Brindabella Hills Winery
reason: One of dozens of Canberra district cellar doors; sources list it among Hall wineries and none singles it out as a destination in its own right (run rule on wineries).
objection: Four counted sources name it and it has views over the Murrumbidgee; but they are lists of wineries, and it opens weekends only.

name: Burns Golf Club Belconnen
reason: A public golf course/club; the run rejects golf clubs (rule 2).
objection: A public course is open to anyone, but no visitor source names it.

name: Canberra Brick Show
reason: an annual event, not a place there whenever a visitor arrives (rule 4)
objection: None.

name: Canberra Cruises and Parties
reason: A boat cruise operator; the lake is the place, not the cruise (COVERAGE: a spot is a place).
objection: None.

name: Canberra Deep Space Communication Complex
reason: Wikivoyage Tuggeranong and Country ACT (read) and six more counted sources: NASA tracking station with a visitor centre with space exhibits, open weekends, free; a named national institution (rules 1-3).
objection: About 45 minutes from Civic, weekend-only opening, and the cafe/shop may be closed.

name: Canberra Museum and Gallery
reason: Wikivoyage Civic (read) lists it: permanent Canberra history gallery and the Sidney Nolan Collection, free, open daily (rule 2).
objection: A modest regional museum; temporary exhibitions are not a lasting draw.

name: Canberra Railway Museum
reason: Wikivoyage South Canberra (read) and VisitCanberra museums list it: historic locomotives including Australia's oldest operating steam locomotive; visitors go in (rule 2).
objection: Volunteer-run with limited open days and hours; a niche interest.

name: Canberra Times Marathon Festival
reason: an annual event, not a place there whenever a visitor arrives (rule 4)
objection: None.

name: Canberra Truffle Festival
reason: Annual seasonal festival (June to August), not a permanent place (rule 4); truffle farms, if wanted, are separate candidates.
objection: None.

name: Capital Region Farmers Market
reason: A weekly Saturday market, not there whenever a visitor arrives (rule 4).
objection: A well-known market, but only one day a week.

name: Captain James Cook Memorial
reason: VisitCanberra attractions and 100-things lists name this lakeside water jet and globe (counted, read); a landmark guides single out beside Lake Burley Griffin, but a lakeside memorial that is a short stop; the jet runs only at set hours.
objection: For: two counted sources, a distinctive landmark visitors photograph at Regatta Point. Against: a memorial and a short visit, with the jet not always running; Wikivoyage Civic treats Civic memorials as not popular destinations.

name: Civic Library
reason: A library and civic building (rule 2); Wikivoyage lists it only as one of the Civic Square buildings.
objection: None.

name: Cockington Green Gardens
reason: Wikivoyage Gungahlin (read) calls it one of Canberra's best-known attractions: miniature English village and international display, train rides, daily 9:30-5; permanent paid attraction (rules 1-4).
objection: Family-oriented and ticketed, so not for every traveller.

name: Commonwealth Park
reason: Wikivoyage Canberra (read) and VisitCanberra name the lakeside park with sculptures, ponds, walkways and an open-air theatre, designed by Dame Sylvia Crowe in 1964; the park is a permanent place and Floriade is only an event held in it (rules 1-4).
objection: Mostly an urban park; its main fame is the Floriade festival, which is not a spot, and the lake edge is covered by other candidates.

name: Corin Forest
reason: Wikivoyage Tuggeranong and Country ACT (read) lists it as the only ski/snow-play resort in the ACT with an alpine slide and snow play, with VisitCanberra's nature reserves page: a permanent recreation venue like a ski field or amusement park (COVERAGE rule 4), kept as a place not an operator.
objection: It is a private commercial resort with a lodge; entry is paid and the snow is seasonal. The script flagged it as an operator.

name: Enlighten Festival
reason: an annual event, not a place there whenever a visitor arrives (rule 4)
objection: None.

name: Evatt Bike Path Little Library
reason: A roadside book exchange box; nothing to do for half an hour (rule 2) and a minor curiosity.
objection: Quirky roadside icons can be kept, but no visitor source names this one.

name: Fairbairn Golf Club
reason: A private golf club (rule 2); the run rejects golf clubs.
objection: None.

name: Federal Golf Club
reason: A private golf club in Red Hill; the run rejects golf clubs.
objection: Its Wikipedia article exists, but views alone do not make it a visitor stop.

name: Gold Creek Village
reason: A shopping and dining precinct whose attractions (Cockington Green, the dinosaur museum, reptile zoo, aviary) are separate places; the village is a wrapper (rule 3) and its shops and restaurants fail rule 2.
objection: Wikivoyage calls it Gungahlin's main visitor draw with three counted sources; but listing it duplicates what it contains.

name: Gungahlin Lakes Golf Club
reason: A golf club; the run rejects golf clubs.
objection: None.

name: Hall
reason: Wikivoyage Canberra/Hall (read) and VisitCanberra give the village its own page with a See section, the 20-site National Trust Hall Heritage Walk and access to wineries and One Tree Hill; the run keeps Hall when a visitor source gives it its own listing. The monthly market is not the reason.
objection: Wikivoyage itself says Hall 'may not have much to see'; a short stop mostly for the heritage walk and cafes.

name: High Court of Australia
reason: Wikivoyage South Canberra (read), VisitCanberra attractions: vast public lobby, three courtrooms open to the public and tours, Mon-Fri; a national institution visitors go in (not seen only from the street).
objection: A courthouse: tours are restricted when the court sits, and it sits inside the Parliamentary Triangle precinct with the other institutions.

name: Hijinx Hotel
reason: A commercial escape-room and game venue (rule 2: a business).
objection: None.

name: Jerrabomberra Wetlands
reason: Wikivoyage South Canberra (read), ACT Parks and VisitCanberra: nature reserve with boardwalks, bird hides and walking tracks, open daily 8-6 (rule 2).
objection: Flat and modest, an hour at most; mostly of interest to birders.

name: Korean War Memorial
reason: Part of Anzac Parade and a minor memorial; no source singles it out as a visit in its own right.
objection: The avenue is covered as one place, which already includes it.
